question.problem: Compute the gradient of the function $f: \mathbb{R}^4 \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ defined by ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14220541/assets/471a898dd8e3dca3d9e0b077a135ac794ef58293dafa33703d23490dd92d12b6.svg) with respect to $\mathbf{x}$ at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14220541/assets/552dda7785a5e118e9ff3afa9bf7e7201e7d3be7454e7e380c42946d60506f31.svg)
question.worked_solution:
Writing ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14220541/assets/e0ec0bd3b3ed1126735e229d153c206900bdff443354b04700379343ab15e876.svg), we have

$$
f(\mathbf{x})= \mathbf{b}^T\mathbf{x}.
$$

The gradient of a function $f(x) = \mathbf{b}^T\mathbf{x}$ with respect to $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ is

$$
\nabla_{\mathbf{x}} f(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{b}.
$$

Therefore, we get
